items.title: feat(id): Rust F12.8 guest SDK + playable rust-counter example (#1065)
items.body: Part of #1065 (the Rust SDK slice; the issue stays open for the second SDK and the component-model/WIT decision, both Drew-owned per the triage on the issue). Queue task 13926. ## What this adds **`pkgs/id/examples/rust-world` — `plaza-sdk`, the Rust guest SDK.** A pure Rust program implements the `World` trait (`init`/`update`/`view`, optional `layout`/`records`/`wants`/`snapshot`/`restore`) and `plaza_guest!` emits all 14 documented Plaza ABI v1 exports with the exact signatures from `examples/roc-world/ABI.md`: model as an opaque pointer, host inputs in `plaza_alloc` memory freed by `plaza_free`, one shared output slot, snapshot/restore as a total pair. Helper modules equal the Roc platform libraries: - `screen` = Screen.roc — cell grid, `boxed`, plain text, and the versioned screen JSON (the Roc `expect` values are reproduced byte-for-byte in tests) - `json` = RocJson.roc — bounded decode (64 KiB / depth 64), number lexemes preserved, first-key `get`, validating encode - `grid` = RocGrid.roc — total, bounds-checked row-major grids - `cap` = RocCap.roc — `r` request sessions, request-document builders, result routing - `text` = RocText.roc — total text helpers **`pkgs/id/examples/rust-counter` — the playable example.** Twin of `roc-counter`: trimmed `inc` increments, boxed 20x3 `count=N` screen, layout widening at 30 columns, `{"count":N}` records, `{}` wants, decimal snapshot with total restore. `build.sh` rebuilds the checked-in `counter.wasm` (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`); the module exports exactly `memory` + the 14 `plaza_*` functions and has no imports. **Conformance:** `rust-counter` joins `CONFORMANCE_MODULES` in `pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs`, so the F12.7 suite — documented export signatures vs ABI.md, ABI version 1, snapshot/restore byte-identical round-trip, records/wants schema validity — now exercises a Rust guest end to end. ## Verification (laptop) - `cargo test` in `rust-world`: 9 passed. In `rust-counter`: 2 passed. - `cargo test --lib sandbox::` in `pkgs/id`: 36 passed, including all five `conformance_*` tests with the rust-counter fixture. - PR checks were QUEUED at open time (fleet CI stall); merging under standing merge authority on this verification. ## Not in this slice The AssemblyScript-vs-Zig second SDK and the Wasm component-model/WIT direction — Drew-owned decisions recorded on #1065. The SDK README states this explicitly: the SDK targets the landed ABI v1 module contract, and its helper APIs do not depend on the raw boundary, so a future component binding can sit under the same `World` trait. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): program ecosystem (share, fork, gallery) first-pass design (#6278)
items.body:
## Summary

First-pass research + design record for the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic: doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/.

- D1 program identity = (author public key, name, version, content hash); same-version/different-hash is a surfaced provenance violation

- #8280 — signed program bundle format + sideload import

items.title: feat(id): F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066)
items.body: ## F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066) Implements the confirmed F12.9 remainder for task 12962, now that the gate has landed: issue #1065 (F12.8 guest SDKs) closed via PR #7891 (merged 2026-11-09T01:03Z), verified fresh at claim time. Before this PR, `pkgs/id/src/world/` had no upgrade module, no migrate export, no versioned program-state snapshot format, and no upgrade runner. ### What lands New module `pkgs/id/src/world/upgrade.rs`, re-exported from `crate::world`: - **Versioned snapshot format for world program state** — `ProgramSnapshot` with a magic + format-version envelope. Format v1 (magic, one version byte, raw state) is still decoded so old snapshots upgrade; everything new is encoded at the current format v2 (version, state length, state, FNV-1a checksum), and the decoded snapshot records the format version it was read from. - **Optional `migrate` export in the guest ABI** — the `MigrateExport` host-side contract: `migrate(state, from_version, to_version) -> Result`. Programs without the export (`None`) keep working under the pre-existing behavior: their state is carried across the upgrade byte-for-byte. - **Probe-first upgrade runner** — `upgrade_program` decodes and migrates a probe copy of the state, re-encodes it at the current snapshot format, and reads it back; the running program's version and snapshot are swapped only if the migrated state round-trips exactly. Any failure (migrate refuses, migrated state over the 4 MiB bound, round-trip mismatch) leaves the old program bit-for-bit unchanged — that is the rollback. ### Exit tests (plan, Phase 12 F12.9) In-module tests, each naming its oracle: - `counter_upgrades_across_a_snapshot_format_change` — a v1 ASCII-decimal counter in a v1 snapshot upgrades to a v2 little-endian counter in a current-format snapshot, same value. - `failing_upgrade_leaves_the_old_program_running` — a deliberately failing `migrate` leaves version and snapshot bytes unchanged. - Plus: current-format round-trip records its version, legacy v1 snapshots still decode, corrupted snapshots are refused, no-`migrate` programs carry state unchanged, oversized migrated state rolls back. Targeted tests run on the laptop before opening (`cargo test --lib world::upgrade`: 7 passed); full verification is CI per fleet policy. ### Scope notes - No F12.8 work (issue #1065, landed separately) and no F12.15 work (issue #558, the downstream consumer of this migration path). - The runner is the transport-independent core seam (alongside the BUILDER-gated program install/upgrade path in `world/mod.rs`); wiring it into a live hot-swap command is follow-up work, not hidden in this PR. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

items.body: Implements **Phase 1** of the F12.15 `id world dev` authoring loop for #5541 (design: `doc/2026-11-01_design_id558.md`). The design's dependency gate is now satisfied — F12.9 #1066 landed via #8031 and F12.8 #1065 is closed — verified fresh this shift before starting. ## What this slice does - **`id world dev DIR`** (sandbox feature): source discovery for an app directory (`main.roc` first, sibling `.roc` files in name order, size-capped reads, validated by the compiler's own bounds), platform resolution from `main.roc`'s declared platform path (or `--platform`), and compilation through the existing bounded compiler engine (`world_compile::compile`). A local dev session grants every module its platform provides; hosted worlds keep their capability ceilings. - **Disposable scratch world**: the compiled module launches into an in-memory `WorldCore` + `WorldHandle` with a sandbox guest — the design's chosen local actor seam. No host is contacted, nothing is installed into a named world, and the scratch state is discarded when the session ends. - `--input TEXT` (repeatable) sends inputs as the dev guest; the command prints one JSON report: source files, seed, module size, compiler diagnostics, source-build provenance, initial view, view after each input, records sequence. ## Verification - `cargo test --lib -- world_dev test_cli_parse_world_dev` — **5 passed** on the laptop. The lifecycle test is the disposability oracle: the checked-in Roc counter starts at `count=0`, applies `inc` inputs through the actor to `count=2`, and a fresh launch starts again at `count=0`. - New module is `rustfmt`-clean; CLI parse test covers the new subcommand. ## Known gap (pre-existing, not this PR) An end-to-end compile of a Roc app cannot run on the laptop today: the platform host build (`examples/roc-world/build-host.sh`) fails on the installed Zig 0.17 (`Optimize.Debug` removed), so `targets/wasm32/host.wasm` cannot be produced. Filed as **#8152**. The compile leg here reuses `world_compile::compile`, which the host `Compile` path already exercises; once #8152 lands, `id world dev pkgs/id/examples/roc-counter --input inc` is the e2e check. ## Follow-ups (later design phases, staying on #5541) Watch/debounce + F12.9 hot-swap via `world::upgrade`, fixture promotion gates (dev-only cross-module-hash replay), deterministic fuzz + declared invariants, latency benchmark + authoring docs. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added `id world dev` for compiling and running an app locally in an offline, disposable environment. * Specify an app directory and optionally a platform, Roc compiler, seed, and ordered text inputs. * View the initial state and the result after each input in a JSON report.

items.title: id(sync): split serve range sessions onto /id-range-sync/1 (#179)
items.body: Fix for #179 (queue task 2970) — both halves, so #179 closes with this PR. ## What changed **1. The split (earlier commits).** `serve`'s range sessions (`event_store::sync`, via `EventSyncProtocol`) opened with a range flight on `/id-sync/1` — the same ALPN as `log_sync` sessions whose first frame is a `Request`/`Answer` handshake, so each side misread the other. Range sessions moved to a distinct ALPN, **`/id-range-sync/1`**, with the split documented in code and in `doc/2026-10-29T16-21-00Z_design_id_sync_alpn_split/`. **2. Range under the handshake (00569c4b).** `log_sync::run_agreed` no longer returns `NotWired` for `SyncMethod::Range`: a Range request agreed under the `Request`/`Answer` handshake now runs a range session on the same stream pair. The store seam is **per-call locking** — the range session is generalised over a new `event_store::sync::RangeStore` trait (sync set / one event's bytes / one ingest batch); `SharedEventStore` takes its `RwLock` per step, never across an await, the same discipline the range session already used internally. The handshake itself now runs on the raw streams; only the `Log` arm wraps them in `Frames`. `sync_method` gains `LogAndRange` support — `LogSyncOnly` responders still refuse Range, and refusal/mismatch semantics are unchanged. `SyncError::NotWired` is removed. Design record: `doc/2026-10-29T16-57-03Z_design_id_sync_range_store_seam/`. New tests: one peer/store pair syncs by Log then by Range under the one handshake (both sides report the agreed method, stores converge after each); a first frame that is not a valid `Request` is refused as a frame error; `LogAndRange` supports both methods. ## Verification CI on this PR (no local builds per fleet CI-first rule). Known blockers unrelated to this change: `main` fmt/clippy breakage fixed by #2335, and the merge-queue stall #1599 — this PR merges once those clear. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Range synchronization can now run through the shared sync handshake when both sides support it. * Sync results distinguish stored-but-voided events from applied events. * **Bug Fixes** * Events refused because a store is frozen are counted as refused, not voided. * **Compatibility** * Range sessions served by `id serve` now use `/id-range-sync/1`; log synchronization continues to use `/id-sync/1`. * **Documentation** * Updated protocol and serving documentation to reflect the distinction between range and log synchronization.

### Compress/s2: Integer Overflow or Wraparound and Out-of-bounds Write in compress
[CVE-2026-63209](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63209) / [GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Signed Integer Overflow in s2.NewDict

##### Summary

A signed integer overflow vulnerability in `s2.NewDict()` allows an attacker to bypass repeat index validation by supplying a dictionary with a uvarint-encoded repeat value exceeding `MaxInt64`. When `Dict.Encode()` is subsequently called, the overflowed negative repeat value causes an out-of-bounds memory access via `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic, crashing the process with SIGSEGV.

##### Package

- **Name:** `github.com/klauspost/compress/s2`
- **Ecosystem:** Go
- **Affected versions:** <= v1.18.6 (all versions with `NewDict` function)

##### Severity

**High (7.5)** — CVSS v3.1: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

##### Vulnerability

##### Type
- CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write (via unsafe.Pointer)

##### Description

The `NewDict()` function reads a uvarint from dictionary data and converts it to `int`:

```go
r, n := binary.Uvarint(dict)
// ...
d.repeat = int(r)
if d.repeat > len(dict) {
    return nil
}
```

When `r` exceeds `MaxInt64` (9223372036854775807), `int(r)` overflows to a negative value. Since a negative number is never greater than a positive length, the validation check is bypassed.

When `Dict.Encode()` is called, the negative `repeat` value causes an integer overflow in `encodeBlockDictGo()`:

```go
repeat := len(dict.dict) - dict.repeat  // overflows: 62 - (-5758978476775341977) = huge positive
candidate := len(dict.dict) - repeat + s // underflows to negative
load32(dict.dict, candidate)             // OOB via unsafe.Pointer
```

`load32` calls `le.Load32` which uses `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic without bounds checking:

```go
func Load32[I Indexer](b []byte, i I) uint32 {
    return *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)), i))
}
```

This causes a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) when the negative index is dereferenced.

##### PoC

```go
package main

import (
    "encoding/binary"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/klauspost/compress/s2"
)

func main() {
    var dictData []byte
    buf := make([]byte, binary.MaxVarintLen64)
    n := binary.PutUvarint(buf, 12687765596934209639) // > MaxInt64
    dictData = append(dictData, buf[:n]...)
    dictData = append(dictData, make([]byte, 16)...) // minimum dict size

    dict := s2.NewDict(dictData)
    // dict is non-nil despite invalid repeat value (overflow bypassed validation)

    src := make([]byte, 64)
    for i := range src { src[i] = byte(i) }
    dict.Encode(nil, src) // SIGSEGV: OOB access via unsafe.Pointer
}
```

##### Impact

- **Denial of Service:** The process crashes immediately with SIGSEGV

##### Attack Vector

Any application that:
1. Accepts user-supplied S2 dictionary data via `s2.NewDict()`
2. Calls `Dict.Encode()` on any data ≥32 bytes

##### Suggested Fix

Validate the uvarint value before converting to int:

```go
if r > math.MaxInt64 {
    return nil
}
d.repeat = int(r)
```

Or use `uint` for the repeat field and validate against `uint(len(dict))`.

##### References

- Source: `s2/dict.go` lines 59-61 (vulnerability), `s2/encode_all.go` line 947 (crash site)
- Commit: 539243b (v1.18.6 + 4 commits)

items.title: mcpx artifacts: opt-in touch-on-read renewal via artifacts.idleTtl (#2548)
items.body: Closes #2548. Queue task 3781 (repo-health-code-pilot). Adopts the touch-on-read TTL convention (docs/decisions/0006-ttl-touch-on-read.md) for mcpx artifacts, in the opt-in form #1884 specified: - **New declared settings** `artifacts.idleTtl` (duration, default `0s` = off) and paired `artifacts.maxAge` (duration, default `168h`), in the settings registry with defaults carried in `internal/defaults/defaults.json`; wired into both store constructors (daemon `routes_exec.go`, CLI `localStore`). Effect-coverage exemptions added in the existing artifact-store style, pin raised 182 → 184. - **Store (`internal/artifacts`)**: new `Options.IdleTTL`/`MaxAge` (a non-positive MaxAge with IdleTTL set falls back to `defaults.ArtifactMaxAge` at Open). When IdleTTL is set, an item read (`Get`, and therefore `OpenBody`/`Bytes`) of a live artifact touches it: `lastTouched = now`, deadline becomes `min(created + maxAge, lastTouched + idleTtl)`, persisted in a new `last_touched` column (added by migration to pre-existing stores; old rows read back with lastTouched = created). Touch never shortens an explicit per-artifact lifetime and never revives an expired artifact. `List` (collection read) does not touch, and `Delete` reads through the non-touching path so GC cannot renew what it enforces. With IdleTTL unset, behaviour is byte-for-byte the old absolute expiry. - **Representation vocabulary**: `Meta` now also carries `expiresAt` (RFC 3339, same instant as the existing `expires`, which stays for existing readers), `lastTouched`, and `ttlRemainingMs` (never negative), restamped on every representation produced. - No `/renew` endpoint or per-resource renew operation is added. - `docs/configuration.md` regenerated from the registry (also refreshes one stale generated row for `tasks.ttl`). ## Tests New targeted tests in `internal/artifacts`: default read does not renew; opt-in read renews to lastTouched + idleTtl and persists; renewal clamped to created + maxAge; collection reads do not touch; touch never shortens an explicit lifetime or revives an expired artifact (GC still collects it). On the laptop: `go test ./internal/artifacts/` passes; `go build ./...` passes. Pre-existing failures on clean main, unchanged by this PR: `internal/defaults` TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault, and `internal/settings` TestEveryDocumentHasAChapter / TestNoUndeclaredEnvRead / TestEverySettingHasAnEffectProbeOrAnExemption (unrelated settings) / TestTheScriptEnvironmentIsWhatTheCodeSets, and `internal/cli` TestStoryDocumentIsCurrent (story.md AGENTS.md line count) — this PR's two new settings have exemptions and are not in that list, and the two generated-doc tests that fail on main pass here after regeneration. 🤖 Queue worker lane E, task 3781. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Artifact retention can now be configured with an idle timeout and a maximum age. By default, idle-based renewal is off, and the maximum age is seven days. * When idle renewal is enabled, reading a live artifact extends its expiry, up to the configured maximum age. Listing artifacts does not renew them, and expired artifacts are not restored. * **Documentation** * Updated configuration guidance to describe the artifact retention settings.
